questions.question: Which scheme is NOT proposed to be covered under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Nidhi?
questions.questionHtml: Which scheme is NOT proposed to be covered under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Nidhi?

options.text: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)
options.html: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)

options.text: Ayushman Bharat - Health and Wellness Centres (AB-HWCs)
options.html: Ayushman Bharat - Health and Wellness Centres (AB-HWCs)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​Rashtriya Swasthya Aashwasan Yojana (RSAY).

questions.question: The Government has launched _________ to encourage the spirit of entrepreneurship in the underserved/unserved areas of India by providing enabling infrastructure and facilitating environment for innovation.
questions.questionHtml: The Government has launched _________ to encourage the spirit of entrepreneurship in the underserved/unserved areas of India by providing enabling infrastructure and facilitating environment for innovation.

options.html: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">Production Linked Incentive Scheme</font></font>
<font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">One Nation One Ration Policy</font></font>
<font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">Atal Community Innovation Centre Programme</font></font>
<font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">Digital Library Mission</font></font>

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Atal Community Innovation Centre ProgrammeKey Points

  • The Atal Community Innovation Centre (ACIC) Programme was launched by the NITI Aayog as part of the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM).
  • The programme is designed to support and promote innovation, entrepreneurship, and the development of local solutions in rural and underserved regions of India.
  • The initiative primarily targets communities that lack access to innovation and entrepreneurial opportunities, such as remote and rural regions.
  • It  emphasizes the use of solution-driven design thinking and a Public Private Partnership (PPP) model to foster innovation and entrepreneurship

Additional Information

  • PLI Scheme (Production-Linked Incentive Scheme):
    • The PLI Scheme is designed to encourage domestic manufacturing and reduce dependency on imports, while also creating job opportunities.
    • It targets various sectors like electronics, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and automotive, providing incentives to companies based on their production levels and investments.
  • One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC):
    • The ONORC scheme is a significant reform under the National Food Security Act (NFSA).
    • It allows ration card holders to access food grains from any Public Distribution System (PDS) shop in the country, ensuring portability for beneficiaries, especially migrant workers and their families.
    • This scheme promotes inclusivity and ensures that no one is deprived of food security due to migration.
  • Digital Library Mission:
    • The Digital Library Mission aims to digitize books, manuscripts, and other knowledge resources to preserve them and make them accessible to people across the world.
    • This initiative promotes learning, research, and cultural heritage preservation through the creation of a vast digital library of resources.
    • It enables easy access to educational materials for people from all walks of life.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (PMGKRA) was launched in the year 2020 by which Ministry of Government of India?
questions.questionHtml: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (PMGKRA) was launched in the year 2020 by which Ministry of Government of India?

options.text: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
options.html: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

options.text: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
options.html: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

options.text: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
options.html: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ministry of Rural Development

Key Points

  • The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (PMGKRA) was launched in the year 2020 by the Ministry of Rural Development of the Government of India.
  • The initiative aims to provide livelihood opportunities to the returnee migrant workers and similarly affected rural citizens due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
  • It focuses on the creation of infrastructure and employment in rural areas, thereby enhancing economic activities.
  • This Abhiyaan covers 116 districts across 6 states, ensuring a broad reach to the affected populace.

Additional Information

  • The PMGKRA was launched on 20th June 2020 as a part of the economic response to COVID-19.
  • The Abhiyaan involves the convergence of 25 different types of works/activities, which will provide employment to the workers.
  • It aims to saturate villages with public infrastructure and create livelihood opportunities in the wake of the pandemic.
  • It is a 125-day campaign with an estimated budget of Rs. 50,000 crore.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the micro-credit scheme ‘Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi’ (‘PM SVANidhi’) launched?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following years was the micro-credit scheme ‘Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi’ (‘PM SVANidhi’) launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2020.

Key Points

  • PM SVANidhi
    • The PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SvaNidhi) was launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs on June 01, 2020.
    • This is a flagship scheme of the Government of India, in line with the guidelines of Atmanirbhar Bharat.
    • It is a special micro-credit facility scheme for providing affordable loans to street vendors.

Additional Information

  • The scheme is aimed at enabling the street vendors to resume their livelihoods that have been adversely affected due to COVID-19 lockdown.
  • The duration of the scheme is until March 2022.
  • HDFC Bank has announced the launch of a micro-credit facility for PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) with common service centres(CSC).
  • The Scheme is available for beneficiaries belonging to only those States/UTs which have notified Rules and Scheme under Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014.

questions.question: In how many categories are loans provided under the MUDRA loan scheme?
questions.questionHtml: In how many categories are loans provided under the MUDRA loan scheme?
questions.solution: The MUDRA loan scheme provides loans under three categories: Shishu, Kishore, and Tarun. Shishu covers loans up to ₹50,000, Kishore covers loans above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5 lakh, and Tarun covers loans above ₹5 lakh and up to ₹10 lakh. Tarun Plus: Rs. 10 lakh and up to Rs. 20 lakhs Launched by the Government of India in April 2015 under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY), the scheme aims to support micro and small enterprises by providing necessary financial assistance. The loans are collateral-free and can be availed from various financial institutions, fostering entrepreneurship and generating employment in the country.

questions.question: PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) Scheme was launched by which ministry?
questions.questionHtml: PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) Scheme was launched by which ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
options.html: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
Key Points

  • PM SVANidhi is a central government scheme that aims to provide financial assistance to street vendors to resume their livelihoods, which were impacted due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
  • The scheme was launched on June 1, 2020, by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA).
  • Under this scheme, street vendors can avail of a working capital loan of up to Rs. 10,000, which is repayable in monthly installments within a year.
  • The scheme targets to benefit over 50 lakh street vendors across the country.
  • The scheme also provides incentives to promote digital transactions among street vendors.

Additional Information

  • Ministry of Consumer Affairs - This ministry is responsible for regulating and promoting consumer interests in the country. It is not directly related to the PM SVANidhi scheme.
  • Ministry of Finance - This ministry is responsible for the management of the country's financial resources. While it might have some indirect involvement in the scheme, it is not the primary ministry responsible for its implementation.
  • Ministry of Commerce - This ministry is responsible for promoting and regulating foreign trade and commerce in the country. It does not have a direct role in the PM SVANidhi scheme.

questions.question: Which of the following helps borrowers to overcome the problem of lack of collateral?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following helps borrowers to overcome the problem of lack of collateral?
questions.solution: Self Help Groups (SHGs) are small, informal groups of poor individuals facing similar problems, who support each other to overcome them. They promote savings among members, which are deposited in a bank, forming a common fund. This fund is used to provide small loans to members without requiring collateral. SHGs are registered under various Societies Acts and play a crucial role in enabling financial inclusion for those lacking traditional collateral.

questions.question: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan is a flagship programme of the government of India, that was started in 2001 to achieve ________.
questions.questionHtml: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan is a flagship programme of the government of India, that was started in 2001 to achieve ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Universalisation of Elementary Education (UEE).

Key Points

  • Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) is the Government of India's flagship program for achieving Universalisation of Elementary Education (UEE).
  • Launched in 2001, SSA aims to provide free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14 years.
  • The program focuses on bridging gender and social gaps in education.
  • SSA is aligned with the mandate of the Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009, which makes education a fundamental right.

Additional Information

  • Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009:
    • Ensures free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 years in India.
    • Mandates 25% reservation for disadvantaged sections in private schools.
    • Sets norms and standards for pupil-teacher ratios, infrastructure, and teacher qualifications.
  • Mid-Day Meal Scheme:
    • Provides free lunches on working days for children in primary and upper primary classes.
    • Aims to improve nutritional status of children and encourage school attendance.
  • National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:
    • Aims to overhaul the Indian education system and improve the quality of education.
    • Focuses on early childhood care and education, foundational literacy, and numeracy.
  • Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA):
    • Launched in 2009 to enhance access to secondary education and improve its quality.
    • Aims to achieve a gross enrollment ratio of 100% in secondary education by 2030.

questions.question: Namami Gange Programme was approved by the Government of India in the year ________.
questions.questionHtml: Namami Gange Programme was approved by the Government of India in the year ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2014.

Key Points

  • Namami Gange Programme was approved in June 2014.
  • ​It was started in 2014.
  • Namami Gange Programme is an Integrated Conservation Mission, approved by the Government of India.

Additional Information

  • It was started with a budget outlay of Rs.20,000 Crore to accomplish the twin objectives of effective abatement of pollution, conservation, and rejuvenation of the National River Ganga.
  • The River Ganga is important not only for its cultural and spiritual significance but also because it hosts more than 40% of the country’s population.
  • 8 states are covered under the project including Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.
  • The main pillars of this programme include Biodiversity, Riverfront Development, Sewage Treatment Infrastructure, River Surface Cleaning, Public Awareness, Afforestation, Ganga Gram and Industrial Effluent Monitoring.

questions.question: Which government scheme’s main aim is to ‘transform rural poor youth into an economically independent and globally relevant workforce’?
questions.questionHtml: Which government scheme’s main aim is to ‘transform rural poor youth into an economically independent and globally relevant workforce’?

options.text: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
options.html: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana

options.text: Deendayal Antyoday Yojana - National Rural Livelihood Mission
options.html: Deendayal Antyoday Yojana - National Rural Livelihood Mission

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya YojanaKey Points

  • Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
    • Grameen Kaushalya Yojana or DDU-GKY is a Government of India youth employment scheme.
    • It was launched on 25 September 2014 by Union Ministers Nitin Gadkari and Venkaiah Naidu on the occasion of 98th birth anniversary of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya.
    • The Vision of DDU-GKY is to "Transform rural poor youth into an economically independent and globally relevant workforce".
    • DDU-GKY has successfully trained thousands of rural youth, providing them with the skills needed to enter various sectors such as construction, retail, hospitality, healthcare, and IT.

Additional Information

  • Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Rurban Mission
    • ​The Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Rurban Mission (SPMRM) is a scheme launched by the Government of India in 2016 under the Ministry of Rural Development.
    • It aims to provide integrated development of rural areas by promoting economic, social, and infrastructural development in rural regions, with the goal of improving the quality of life and creating sustainable livelihoods in rural areas.
    • The mission promotes PPP models to foster the involvement of both public and private stakeholders in the development of rurban clusters
  • Deendayal Antyoday Yojana - National Rural Livelihood Mission 
    • ​Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihood Mission (DAY-NRLM) is a government initiative launched by the Ministry of Rural Development in 2011 to reduce poverty and enhance the livelihood opportunities of the rural poor in India.
    • The mission primarily focuses on empowering rural women through self-help groups (SHGs), improving their economic status, and fostering social inclusion.
    • The scheme prioritizes women’s empowerment by organizing rural women into self-help groups (SHGs).

questions.question: Which of the following has initiated the Village Defence Guards scheme to instil a sense of self protection and ensure the safety and security of villages and infrastructural installations in and around the villages?

  • Jammu and Kashmir has initiated the Village Defence Guards scheme.

  • The Village Defence Guards are trained to handle emergency situations and provide immediate assistance in case of any threats to the community.
  • This initiative is part of the broader efforts to enhance security and empower local communities in Jammu and Kashmir.

  • The Village Defence Guards scheme is a continuation of earlier measures to involve local communities in maintaining law and order in the region.
  • Such initiatives are crucial for the socio-economic development of the region, ensuring that peace and stability are maintained.
  • In addition to security, the scheme also aims to build trust between the local population and the authorities.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the ‘EShakti’ programme?
questions.questionHtml: What is the purpose of the ‘EShakti’ programme?

options.text: Digitisation of Self-Help Group details for banks
options.html: Digitisation of Self-Help Group details for banks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the Digitisation of Self-Help Group details for banksKey Points

  • The E-Shakti program was launched by the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) to digitize Self Help Groups (SHGs) in India.
  • The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) initiated the digitising of Self Help Groups (SHGs) in India through their pilot project called e-Shakti.

questions.question: The National Rural Employment Programme was merged with _________ in 1989.
questions.questionHtml: The National Rural Employment Programme was merged with _________ in 1989.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jawahar Rozgar Yojana.

Key Points

  • Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) was launched on April 1, 1989, by merging National Rural Employment Programme and Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme by Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.
  • The urban version of this program was Nehru Rozgar Yojana.
  • This was a consolidation of the previous employment programs and it was the largest National Employment Program of India at that time with a general objective of providing 90-100 Days of Employment per person particularly in backward districts.
  • People below Poverty Line were the main targets.
  • The Yojna was implemented on a rural scale.
  • Every village was to be covered through Panchayati Raj Institutions.
  • The village got aid and support from District Rural Development Authority.
  • Expenditures were born by central & state in 80:20 ratios.​

Additional Information

Program Name Launch Year
Indira Awas Yojana 1985
Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme 1983
Employment Assurance Scheme 1993

questions.question: Under the Sukanya Samriddhi Account Yojana, minimum how much money needs to be deposited in one financial year?
questions.questionHtml: Under the Sukanya Samriddhi Account Yojana, minimum how much money needs to be deposited in one financial year?
questions.solution: The Sukanya Samriddhi Account Yojana requires a minimum annual deposit of Rs. 250. This scheme aims to help parents save for their girl child's education and marriage. Deposits must be in multiples of Rs. 50, with a maximum limit of Rs. 1.5 lakh per year. Accounts can be opened from the birth of the girl until she is 10 years old. Launched under the 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' campaign, the scheme offers an attractive interest rate, tax benefits under Section 80C, and tax-exempt interest and maturity amounts. The account matures after 21 years or upon the girl’s marriage post 18 years, with partial withdrawals allowed for higher education or marriage.

questions.question: The Kisan Credit Card Scheme was introduced in which year by Indian banks?
questions.questionHtml: The Kisan Credit Card Scheme was introduced in which year by Indian banks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1998.

The Kisan Credit Card Scheme was introduced in 1998.

Additional Information

  •  The Kisan Credit Card scheme is a Government of India scheme which provides farmers with timely access to credit.
  • The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme was launched in 1998 with the aim of providing short-term formal credit to farmers.
  • The KCC scheme was prepared by NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) on the recommendations of the R. V. Gupta Committee.
  • The KCC scheme was introduced to ensure that the credit requirements for farmers in the agriculture, fisheries, and animal husbandry sectors were being met.
  • This was done by helping them avail short-term loans and provide them with a credit limit to purchase equipment and for their other expenses as well.
  • The KCC scheme is being implemented by all Co-operative banks, Regional Rural Banks, and Public Sector Banks throughout the country.
  • The validity period is five years, with an option to extend for up to three more years.
  • Kisan Credit Card (KCC) offering credit to the farmers in two types:
    • Cash Credit.
    • Term Credit.
  • The rate of interest on this type of loan is also considerably low compared to agriculture term loan under the scheme farmers have the option of rescheduling the repayment
  • Moreover, with the help of KCC, farmers are exempt from the high interest rates of the regular loans offered by banks as the interest rate for KCC starts as low as 2% and averages at 4%.
  • With the help of this scheme, farmers can repay their loans depending on the harvesting period of their crop for which the loan was given.
  • On 14th May 2020, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced a concessional credit of Rs 2 lakh crore to benefit 2.5 crore farmers through the Kisan Credit Card scheme.
  • The government will undertake a special drive to provide this credit to PM-KISAN beneficiaries through the Kisan Credit Card.

questions.question: President Smt. Droupadi Murmu launched ‘Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan’ in Sep 2022 to eliminate TB from India by which of the following years?
questions.questionHtml: President Smt. Droupadi Murmu launched ‘Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan’ in Sep 2022 to eliminate TB from India by which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2025.

Key Points

  • President Droupadi Murmu virtually launched the Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan to reinvigorate the mission of TB elimination from the country by 2025. 
  • Prime Minister Narendra Modi had given the clarion call to end TB in the country five years ahead of the Sustainable Development Goals of 2030 at the Delhi End TB Summit in March 2018. 
  • During the event, President Murmu also launched the Ni-kshay Mitra initiative, a portal to provide a platform for donors to provide various forms of support to those undergoing TB treatment.

Additional Information

  • Each year, World Tuberculosis (TB) Day is commemorated on March 24 to raise public awareness about the devastating health, social and economic consequences of TB, and to step up efforts to end the global TB epidemic.
  • The date marks the day in 1882 when Dr Robert Koch announced that he had discovered the bacterium (Mycobacterium tuberculosis). that causes TB, which opened the way towards diagnosing and curing this disease.

questions.question: The National Food Security Act was passed in the year _________.
questions.questionHtml: The National Food Security Act was passed in the year _________.
questions.solution:
• The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was passed in the year 2013.

 Key PointsSalient Features-

  • It is also called Right to Food Act.
  • It aims at providing food grains at subsidised rates.
  • Up to 75% of the rural population and 50% of the urban population will be covered under TPDS (Targeted Public Distribution System).
  • It changed the ongoing food security schemes into a legal entitlement and a Right.
  • It includes the Midday Meal Scheme, Integrated Child Development Services scheme and the Public Distribution System. 
  • The beneficiaries of the Public Distribution System (or, PDS) are entitled to 5 kilograms per person per month (excluding beneficiaries of Antodaya Anna Yojana) of cereals at the following prices:-
  • Rice at ₹3 per kg, Wheat at ₹2 per kg, coarse grains (millet) at ₹1 per kg.
  • Antodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) includes poorest of the poor and provide 35 Kg of food grains per household.
  • Pregnant women and lactating mothers and children in the age group of 6 months to 14 years are entitled to meals as per prescribed nutritional norms under Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) and Mid-Day Meal (MDM) schemes.

questions.question: The Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rojgar Yojana (SJSRY) was launched in the year ________ by Government of India.
questions.questionHtml: The Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rojgar Yojana (SJSRY) was launched in the year ________ by Government of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1997

Key Points

  • The Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rojgar Yojana (SJSRY) was launched in the year 1997 by the Government of India.
  • SJSRY is aimed at providing gainful employment to the urban unemployed and underemployed poor by encouraging the setting up of self-employment ventures or provision of wage employment.
  • The scheme focuses on providing skill development training to the urban poor to enhance their employability.
  • It also includes support for the establishment of micro-enterprises by urban poor women and youth.
  • The implementation of the scheme is done by urban local bodies (ULBs) with the support of state governments.

Additional Information

  • The scheme was restructured and subsumed into the National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM) in 2013.
  • SJSRY had five major components: Urban Self-Employment Programme (USEP), Urban Wage Employment Programme (UWEP), Skill Training for Employment Promotion amongst Urban Poor (STEP-UP), Urban Women Self-help Programme (UWSP), and Urban Community Development Network (UCDN).
  • The focus of the scheme was to provide sustainable livelihood opportunities through skill development and micro-enterprises, with a special emphasis on women and vulnerable sections of society.
  • Under the scheme, urban local bodies were encouraged to form community structures such as self-help groups (SHGs) and community development societies (CDSs) to facilitate the implementation of the program.

questions.question: According to the National Population Policy 2000, what is the target year for reaching stability in population?
questions.questionHtml: According to the National Population Policy 2000, what is the target year for reaching stability in population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2045.

Key Points

  • The National Population Policy 2000 was formulated by the Government of India to address the issues of population growth and reproductive health.
  • The policy aims to achieve a stable population by the year 2045, consistent with the requirements of sustainable economic growth, social development, and environmental protection.
  • The policy includes objectives such as the reduction of infant mortality rate and maternal mortality rate, and promotion of contraceptive methods.
  • It emphasizes universal access to quality health care services, including family planning and reproductive health services.
  • Educational programs and awareness campaigns are crucial components of the policy to ensure informed choices regarding family planning.

Additional Information

  • Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)
    • IMR refers to the number of infant deaths (under one year) per 1,000 live births in a given year.
    • Reducing the IMR is a key objective of the National Population Policy 2000.
  • Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR)
    • MMR refers to the number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births due to complications from pregnancy or childbirth.
    • The policy aims to bring down the MMR through improved healthcare services.
  • Contraceptive Methods
    • These include various methods and devices used to prevent pregnancy, ensuring family planning and reproductive health.
    • The policy promotes the use of contraceptives to control population growth.
